name: Airbnb
summary: Practice string, file-system, and graph-ordering problems often seen in Airbnb-style interview prep.

questions.title: Palindrome Pairs
questions.summary: Find all ordered pairs of words that form a palindrome when concatenated.
questions.prompt: Given a list of unique words, return every pair of distinct indexes where words[i] plus words[j] is a palindrome.

examples.explanation: bat + tab and tab + bat are palindromes.

constraints: Pairs are ordered and indexes must be distinct.

solutionTracks.title: Hash Map Split Check
solutionTracks.summary: Try every split in every word and use a reversed-word map to find a partner for the non-palindrome side.

steps.title: Map words to indexes
steps.explanation: A hash map finds whether the reverse of a needed fragment exists.

steps.title: Split every word
steps.explanation: Each cut creates a left and right fragment. One fragment may be the palindrome middle.

steps.title: Emit both orientations
steps.explanation: If the left is palindrome, a reversed right can go before; if the right is palindrome, a reversed left can go after.

solutionTracks.explanation: For word A plus word B to be a palindrome, the unmatched portion after mirrored comparison must already be palindromic. Splitting enumerates every possible unmatched portion.

solutionTracks.title: Reverse Trie With Palindrome Suffixes
solutionTracks.summary: Insert reversed words into a trie and store indexes where the remaining prefix is already a palindrome.

steps.title: Build reversed trie
steps.explanation: Each word is inserted backward so searching a forward word compares mirrored characters.

steps.title: Record palindrome leftovers
steps.explanation: At each trie node, store word indexes whose unconsumed prefix is a palindrome.

steps.title: Search each word
steps.explanation: When the search ends or hits a word boundary, use palindrome checks to emit valid pairs.

solutionTracks.explanation: A pair forms a palindrome when the matched mirrored parts are equal and the leftover part on either side is itself a palindrome. The trie organizes those mirrored comparisons efficiently.

complexity.time: O(total characters squared for palindrome checks)

questions.title: In-Memory File System
questions.summary: Design a small file system API with directory listing and file content operations.
questions.prompt: Implement ls, mkdir, addContentToFile, and readContentFromFile for an in-memory file system rooted at slash.

examples.explanation: The file c is inside directory /a/b.

constraints: Directory listings should be returned in lexicographic order.

diagrams.title: Path tree
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  R[/] --> A[a]
  A --> B[b]
  B --> C[c file]

solutionTracks.title: Path Trie
solutionTracks.summary: Represent directories as trie nodes and keep optional file contents on nodes that are files.

steps.title: Split paths
steps.explanation: Break a path into non-empty parts so each part becomes one trie edge.

steps.title: Create directories lazily
steps.explanation: mkdir and addContent create missing nodes along the path.

steps.title: Separate listing behavior
steps.explanation: ls returns a single filename for file nodes or sorted child names for directory nodes.

solutionTracks.explanation: A trie matches the hierarchy of a file system: each node owns its children and possibly file content. Walking path parts reaches exactly the requested location.

solutionTracks.title: Flat Path Maps
solutionTracks.summary: Store directories and files in separate maps keyed by full path for a compact MVP implementation.

steps.title: Track directory children
steps.explanation: A directory map stores sorted names for each directory path.

steps.title: Track file content
steps.explanation: A file map stores content by complete file path.

steps.title: Update parents on create
steps.explanation: Whenever a path is created, add its final name to the parent directory child set.

solutionTracks.explanation: Full path keys avoid building node objects. This is simple and effective when path normalization is controlled by the prompt.

questions.title: Alien Dictionary
questions.summary: Infer a valid character order from words sorted by an unknown alphabet.
questions.prompt: Given words sorted according to an unknown alphabet, return one valid ordering of the characters or an empty string if the ordering is impossible.

examples.explanation: Adjacent word differences imply w before e, r before t, and t before f.

constraints: A longer word before its own prefix is invalid.

solutionTracks.title: Topological Sort From Adjacent Words
solutionTracks.summary: Compare adjacent sorted words to infer character precedence edges, then topologically sort the graph.

steps.title: Initialize every character
steps.explanation: Even characters with no edges must appear in the output.

steps.title: Compare neighboring words
steps.explanation: The first differing character between adjacent words gives one ordering edge.

steps.title: Run topological sort
steps.explanation: Kahn BFS emits characters with zero indegree and detects cycles or contradictions.

solutionTracks.explanation: The sorted dictionary only reveals precedence at the first differing character between neighboring words. Topological sort combines all those local constraints into one valid alphabet order.

solutionTracks.title: DFS Topological Order
solutionTracks.summary: Build the same precedence graph, then use DFS colors to detect cycles while appending completed characters.

steps.title: Build graph edges
steps.explanation: Adjacent word comparisons create directed edges from earlier characters to later characters.

steps.title: Color during DFS
steps.explanation: Visiting a gray node means the ordering constraints contain a cycle.

steps.title: Reverse completed order
steps.explanation: Characters are appended after descendants finish, so reversing gives dependency-first order.

solutionTracks.explanation: DFS postorder places each prerequisite after its outgoing descendants, so reversing postorder creates a valid topological order when no cycle exists.
